title: Forces and Motion (KS4 Physics)
subject: Physics
strapline: Balanced and unbalanced forces, and the key equations.
facts: A force is a push or pull, measured in newtons (N); forces can be contact or non-contact.
When forces on an object are balanced, it stays still or moves at constant velocity (Newton’s first law).
A resultant (unbalanced) force causes acceleration: force = mass × acceleration (F = ma).
Weight = mass × gravitational field strength (W = mg); on Earth g ≈ 9.8 N/kg.
Speed = distance ÷ time; velocity is speed in a given direction.
Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time taken.
Newton’s third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

quick_quiz.q: State the equation linking force, mass and acceleration.
What is the unit of force?
If forces are balanced, what happens to a moving object?
quick_quiz.a: it keeps moving at constant velocity

teacher_tips: Distinguish mass (kg, constant) from weight (N, depends on gravity).
Practise rearranging F = ma in all three forms.
Use free-body diagrams to decide if forces are balanced.
